clue.text: 5 across, or 24

definitions.meaning: the designer Gianni Versace was murdered in 1997, so the famous name was itself a casualty in the world of style
a mink is killed for its fur so that coats can be made, an animal sacrificed to style

explanation.surface: A puzzling cross-reference asking what a designer and a fur-bearing animal have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Both cross-referenced answers fit the phrase: Gianni Versace was shot dead, and minks are farmed and killed for fur coats.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone slavishly following trends; here it is read literally as one who suffers or dies because of style.

clue.text: Partners to ram into newspaper at least

indicators.note: the partners go into the newspaper, so these letters sit inside the paper's abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
a ram's mates are ewes

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about mating sheep, featured as little as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the fewest of something is having the least number of it, an equivalent superlative.

clue.text: Israeli king loses a brown sovereign

indicators.note: the king loses a letter, so it is taken out of his name

parts.note: Saul was the first king of Israel
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A biblical king forfeits a brown coin, a sovereign being an old British gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also a British gold coin, which is what the surface pretends; here it means a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is a Muslim ruler, so he is a sovereign in the sense of a monarch.

clue.text: Examiner's job is to replace sign around what helps to create jam

indicators.note: the rearranged letters of sign are wrapped around the jam ingredient
to re-place the letters of sign is to set them down in a new order

parts.note: pectin is the setting agent that makes jam gel

explanation.surface: An examiner's task said to involve swapping a sign round something used in jam-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' shuffles the sign into INSG; 'around' means the jam-setter sits between its S and G. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspecting is the activity of examination, what an examiner does as a job.

clue.text: Children's favourite teacher turns up with empty diary

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: an empty diary keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A teacher arrives with nothing written in a diary, a picture of a children's favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: NODDY is Enid Blyton's little wooden boy from Toyland, a long-running British children's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddy is a famous British children's book and television character, much loved by young readers.

clue.text: Partner of vice, church designer

parts.note: the phrase vice versa pairs the two words
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Vice's partner and a church come together in a fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni Versace founded the Italian fashion house, so he is a famous example of a designer.

clue.text: Pass round university and face up to what's seen to be helpful

indicators.note: the pass goes round the university, holding its letter inside

parts.note: a visa is a pass for entering a country

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: dial is slang for the face

explanation.surface: Instructions about taking a pass round campus and facing up to things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DIAL into LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual aid is a chart or picture shown to help understanding, literally something seen that helps.

clue.text: Scrummy game involving love and kiss a basis for sauce

indicators.note: the game takes in love, so the letter for nil sits inside

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game with scrums
love means nil in tennis, written O
X is the conventional sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A rugby match featuring love and kisses forms the base of a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux of cooked flour and butter is the thickening base for many sauces.

clue.text: Brilliance of wandering star, one held to move heaven and earth

indicators.note: the shuffled star holds the numeral, which sits inside it
letters that wander move about into a different order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to move heaven and earth is to try very hard

explanation.surface: The brilliance of a roving star, someone determined to do everything possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns STAR into ARTS, and 'held' puts I inside to give ARTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is skill or brilliance in a creative field, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Backs back with those eating 'ay?

parts.note: the end is the back of something
horses eat hay; the dropped H of 'ay is dropped from them too, in Cockney fashion

explanation.surface: A Cockney-flavoured question about animals eating hay at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ay signals the dropped H, so the hay-eaters lose their H as well.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to back or support, so 'backs' is the same verb in the same form.

clue.text: See 10
Letters of worst ugliness, befuddled git their creator?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are to be taken and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: Complaining letters about the worst ugliness, written by a muddled fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddled' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the 25 letters; 'Letters of' does the rearranging. The name is the stock pseudonym of an outraged writer to newspapers from a genteel town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The pseudonym stands for the indignant middle-class correspondent who writes angry letters to the press, the creator of such letters.

clue.text: Chicken appeared tender stuffed into tree, needing no more temperature

indicators.note: the tender part is stuffed inside the shortened tree
no more says that the word more is removed from the tree

parts.note: the sycamore is a tree
taken as written
to have cared is to have shown tenderness

explanation.surface: Instructions for stuffing a tender chicken into a tree, without the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeared tender' is a loose phrase for having shown care. 'no' removes the more, leaving SYCA; the tender part goes in after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken is a coward in slang, and a scaredy-cat is a childish name for a coward.

clue.text: The Guardian and the Queen are sort of friendly?

parts.note: in the newspaper's own crossword the Guardian speaks of itself as us
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Asks whether the newspaper and the monarch get along.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a part phrase: the answer completes 'user-friendly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before friendly, the word forms user-friendly, so it names that particular sort of friendliness.

clue.text: Interpret stake pocketed by the poor

indicators.note: the reading and the stake are pocketed, held inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
to read is to interpret
a stake and a bar are both rigid poles

explanation.surface: An instruction to interpret a stake taken by the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the poor' reads as a noun phrase, but the is the container and poor is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare clothing is worn thin, so the word means poor, shabby or meagre.

clue.text: Deception of Raj, or honest deception?

indicators.note: the letters are dishonestly disguised, a deceit into another order

parts.note: used as written
used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: Was British rule in India a deception, or was it honest?
explanation.walkthrough: The same word serves as definition and anagram signal at either end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden horse of Troy was the classic ruse, so its name stands for any deception from within.

clue.text: Devious fraud virtually concealed by extra supplication

indicators.note: the twisted letters are hidden inside the word for extra

parts.note: an extra one is another

indicators.note: devious means taking a winding course, so the letters are twisted
virtually means almost, so the word is taken without its last letter

explanation.surface: A devious fraud, all but hidden inside an extra plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' leaves FRAU; 'Devious' twists that to URFA, which 'concealed by' places just after the first letter of the extra.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer, known by its opening words, is the best-known Christian supplication.

clue.text: Those associating with criminal types

parts.note: cons are convicts, criminals
sorts are types

explanation.surface: People who keep company with criminal sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal types' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a companion, so those who associate with someone are consorts.

clue.text: Gold in firm can be banked

indicators.note: the gold goes in the firm, its letters placed inside

parts.note: stable means firm and steady
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold held by a firm can be deposited at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Something storable can be put away, and to bank something is to put it into storage.

clue.text: See 10
See 1 across
Noncombatant, though heartless and impulsive?

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its central letter

parts.note: a neutral country takes no side in a war

explanation.surface: A peaceful bystander who is cold yet acts on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impulsive?' is cryptic: the answer concerns nerve impulses, not rash behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Neural means relating to nerves, which work by electrical impulses, hence whimsically impulsive.

clue.text: Recent killer of old emperors reported

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: tsars were the emperors of Russia

explanation.surface: A recent killing of former emperors is announced in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: SARS was the respiratory disease outbreak of 2002-03, recent when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe acute respiratory syndrome was a deadly virus that spread in the early 2000s.

clue.text: Barrier providing cutting message?

definitions.meaning: a fence of spiked strands keeps people or animals out
a barbed remark is cutting, and a wire was a telegram, so a sharp telegram

explanation.surface: A fence that also delivers a sharp telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiked fencing wire is a barrier, and taken as words it is a hurtful telegram.

clue.text: Troubled head of school gripped by alternative to cane

indicators.note: the school's head is gripped, held inside the sugar plant

parts.note: sugar comes from beet as an alternative to sugar cane

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A troubled headteacher held by a replacement for the cane.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests corporal punishment in schools, but the cane is sugar cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Beset means troubled or harassed, as in beset by worries.

clue.text: Useful for keeping some warm in Knightsbridge?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something to keep a wealthy shopper warm in a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Knightsbridge is an expensive area of London, home of Harrods, where fur coats would be worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mink fur makes warm coats, so it is useful for keeping someone warm, as the whole clue suggests.

clue.text: Criticises bishops with one in tears

indicators.note: the bishops and one go in the tears, inside the word

parts.note: to tear along is to rush
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Criticising bishops while one of them is crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping but is the verb for rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish something is to criticise it harshly, informally.

clue.text: Gaul, having lost 9, makes bloomer

indicators.note: the Gaul loses nine, so those letters are removed from his name

parts.note: Asterix is the cartoon Gaul
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Gaul who has lost nine of something makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a daisy-like flower, and a bloomer is something that blooms.

clue.text: One moving stealthily on foot in America

definitions.meaning: in American English this is a soft rubber-soled shoe, worn on the foot

explanation.surface: A creeping figure, walking across America.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sneaks is one moving furtively, and in the US the word is a trainer or plimsoll.

clue.text: Time for Mahler composition, one currently uplifting?

indicators.note: a composition puts the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Time for an inspiring piece by the composer Mahler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' refers to air currents: a rising column of warm air lifts gliders and birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising current of warm air, so it uplifts by means of a current.
